card.name: Words after verbs of bringing into state
card.fires_on: Small words like 'into' or 'un-' right after a verb such as raised, brought, come, get or gone, in older or literary prose. They begin an idiom about entering a state, like 'into fashion' or 'unheeded'.

modes.label: into after a verb
modes.description: The word 'into' follows a verb of moving something or someone into a state or place.
modes.example: put a stop to the political preachings which the League had brought<< into>> fashion.

modes.label: un- start of a word
modes.description: The start of an 'un-' verb or adjective follows a verb or phrase, as in 'gone unheeded'.
modes.example: largely gone<< un>>heeded and unrewarded to the

modes.label: other idiom openers
modes.description: A word such as get, most, his or gentle starts a set phrase after a verb.
modes.example: did not want "the United States to<< get>> the reputation of outdoing Hitler in atrocities

card.plain: It marks the little word in an idiom like 'brought into fashion' or 'gone unheeded' in older prose.
